fresh_candidate_checkout.method: Narrow detached checkout of exact candidate commit; actual file bytes and every committed candidate blob verified against the sealed manifest.

review_scope.note: Completed source, build and visual reviews are bound in the manifest. Fresh-checkout checks do not constitute new mathematical or visual review.

limitations: Command exits: The first run's public build-execution.json was overwritten by the second execution. Its first private receipt retains a hash (3D8535456F2D9E03CF9547CD56EC6F71314A38ED4721DB2DA2D9B43A29652A0D), but not those original JSON bytes. Therefore first per-command exit codes are control-flow-supported, not individually re-read from a preserved first execution manifest.

FLS evidence: 36 generated input occurrences were not retained: each groupoids phase has its .aux/.out/.toc/.bbl; each spaces-perfect phase also reads groupoids.aux. Historical hashes remain in inventories and agree across builds, but those deleted generated bytes cannot be independently rehashed now. Recorded TeX FLS is not a complete separate BibTeX .bib/.bst dependency manifest. This review does not claim a self-contained archived toolchain or full build input bundle.

Mutex and process ownership: Chronology is from the actual wrapper receipt plus reviewed process-creation/control flow and Job Object accounting. There is no per-engine PID/timestamp OS trace, and no new hard-kill, contention, or abandoned-owner fault test was run. Build execution JSON times are rounded to whole seconds; precise wrapper timestamps govern ordering.

Warnings and layout: Standalone cross-chapter references remain unresolved. Groupoids retains the authority's label-rerun warning, so fixed-point AUX convergence is not established by the fixed three-pass recipe. Spaces-perfect retains one identical BibTeX missing-pages warning. Visual pages and mathematical correctness are reviewed separately by root/current source reviewer.

Validator coverage: build-receipt.py records box counts but does not fail on their regression; it also does not classify local versus external targets or test generic label-rerun warnings. Its validate_fls checks advertised structure and source hash but does not recompute the closure digest or require all generated dependencies to be retained. deterministic-replay.py compares advertised closure hashes; this audit recomputed them.
